basis: Tumour arises in the testis, a reproductive organ; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish involvement of skeletal muscle.
Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis with anemia and abnormal red-cell morphology.
Inflammation of the tongue; oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis. An immune mechanism is not established.
Coxsackievirus infection umbrella; neurologic, cardiac, airway and mucocutaneous manifestations vary by syndrome without common lasting damage across the group.
Degeneration of lumbar intervertebral disks; nerve damage is not required or established in at least 30%.
Poliovirus infection destroys spinal motor neurons, producing paralysis; paralysis alone does not establish direct skeletal muscle disease.
Infantile myofibromas characteristically occupy skin, subcutis and musculoskeletal soft tissues; visceral involvement is a minority pattern.
Developmental impairment is common in constitutional 11q deletion syndromes; platelet, cardiac, dental and hearing abnormalities vary with the deleted interval.
Cutaneous thrombo-obliterative vasculopathy; intestinal infarction, hemorrhage and perforation occur in 30-79%. Neurologic and other visceral damage is generally under 30%.
Congenital structural malformation of the mitral valve.
Temporary occlusion of a retinal artery defines an ocular vascular disorder; lasting retinal injury is not required for these primary labels.
Carcinoma originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; histology does not establish another organ site.
Clonal plasma-cell neoplasm explicitly lacking organ impairment; bone and kidney injury would indicate progression beyond smoldering disease.
Isolated failure of sperm production is reproductive; elevated FSH is a compensatory finding rather than evidence of endocrine gland damage.
Fluoride-induced developmental damage to dental enamel; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Skeletal fluorosis is a separate condition.
Inherited iron-transport disorder defined by hypochromic microcytic anemia and progressive hepatic iron overload, independent of transfusion effects.
Teratoma originates in the central nervous system; differentiated tissue components do not imply disease in their corresponding organs.
Umbrella of congenital cerebral cortical malformations; additional skeletal, skin or metabolic abnormalities are subtype dependent.
Congenital vaginal obstruction and associated uterine abnormalities affect reproductive structures outside the axes; abdominal pain and masses add no axis.
Immune-mediated medium-artery vasculitis; cutaneous disease predominates among single-organ cases, supporting skin involvement in at least about 30%. Other sites vary.
Congestive cardiomyopathy attributed to selenium deficiency combined with Coxsackievirus infection; cardiac, infectious and nutritional-metabolic mechanisms define it.
Angiosarcoma originates in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis; endothelial histology alone does not imply additional cardiovascular disease.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%, with deformities and contractures in 30-79%. Laryngeal dysfunction from vocal cord paresis occurs in 30-79%.
Cerebellar malformation, developmental disability and dental anomalies define it; scoliosis and slender bones occur in 6/6, delayed skeletal maturation in 4/6. Sparse hair alone lacks damage.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder causing skeletal myopathy. Restrictive ventilation in 30-79% reflects respiratory muscle weakness without established intrinsic lung damage.
